summary: On a restyled deck a capacity violation ends a slide without a repair call only when it measures the slide over its text budget; a violation naming an element that ended up invisible, clipped or off-canvas is a layout defect the repair call fixes.
invariants: An ordinary authored deck, which owns all of its text, keeps the original classification unchanged.
A restyled slide measured over its budget (visible_text, body, title, images) stays terminal: verbatim source text cannot be shortened to fit.
A restyled slide whose violation names elements is classified by the safety gate instead, which the caller allows into the repair cycle.
A violation this cannot resolve to element names is treated as a budget measurement, so the fail-closed classification is the default.
Safety issues are still reported in the violations either way; only the code changes.
forbidden: End a deck without a repair call because one element was laid out badly.
Let a restyled page that is genuinely over its text budget reach a repair call that could only fix it by deleting source text.
rationale: Operation 3d0b9e72 authored 35 of 35 slides and was ended by slide 16's hero mark: a '+' ornament the browser could not see, clipped, and overlapping the source block beside it.

Operation 069c620d authored, rendered and persisted 35 of 35 and was ended by one clipped source block on page 13, whose entire source is 168 characters across 8 blocks. Nothing was over budget; the slide was laid out badly.
Capacity is terminal because verbatim source text cannot be shortened. That is a statement about the slide's budget, not about which element ended up invisible.
